summary: The root مكن (mkn) means to establish, settle, or assign a place to someone. It also signifies giving someone mastery, dominion, or power over something, enabling them to control or possess it.
lane: 2 مَكَّنَهُ ذ He gave him a place: (Jel, vi. 6:) he assigned him a place, and settled, or established, him. (Bd, ibid, where see more.) You say also, مَكَّنَ لَهُ فِى مَنْزِلٍ [ He assigned, or gave, him a place in an abode ]. (S in art. بوأ .) -b2- مَكَّنَهُ مِنْ شَىْءٍ , and , He made him to have mastery, or dominion, or ascendancy, or authority, and power, over a thing; (Msb;) put it in his power. -b3- مَكَّنَهُ مِنَ الشَّىْءِ , and مِنْهُ , He empowered him, enabled him, or rendered him able, to do the thing: he enabled him to have the thing within his power. Ex. يَدَيْهِ مِنْ رُكْبَتَيْهِ He enabled his hands to take and grasp his knees. from a trad. (Mgh.)

headwords.def: مَكَّنَهُ He gave him a place: (Jel, vi. 6:) he assigned him a place, and settled, or established, him. (Bd, ibid, where see more.) You say also, مَكَّنَ لَهُ فِى مَنْزِلٍ [ He assigned, or gave, him a place in an abode ]. (S in art. بوأ.) مَكَّنَهُ مِنْ شَىْءٍ, and, He made him to have mastery, or dominion, or ascendancy, or authority, and power, over a thing; (Msb;) put it in his power.

أَمْكَنَهُ مِنْ شَىْءِ He made him to have a thing within his power, or reach: enabled him to do, reach, get, or obtain, a thing. See 2. أَمْكَنَهُ It was within his power, or reach; was possible, or practicable, to him. أَمْكَنَهُ It became easy to him. (Msb.) It (an object of the chase) offered him an opportunity to shoot it or capture it; or became within his power, or reach. أَمْكِنِى, said to a woman, [meaning Empower thou; i. e. grant thou access; ] occurs in a poem. (S, art.

تَمَكَّنَ i. q. اِسْتَقَرَّ: (Msb, art. قر:) it is very often used in this sense, as meaning He, or it, settled; became fixed, or established; it became fixed, or steady, in its place; when said of a man, particularly implying in authority and power: see قَرَّ. تَمَكَّنَ مِنْ شَىْءٍ, and, He became possessed of mastery, or dominion, or ascendancy, or authority, and power, over a thing; he was able to avail himself of it: [ he was, or became, within reach of him, or it.
اِسْتَمْكَنَ: see 5. He, or it, was, or became, firm. It seems sometimes to mean It (a plant) took firm root.
مُكْنَةٌ, (Msb, TA,) with damm, (TA,) Power; (Msb, * TA;) ability; (TA;) strength. (Msb.)
مَكِنَةٌ i. q. تَمَكُّنُ. (Sh, TA.) النَّاسُ عَلَى مَكِنَاتِهِمْ means على مَقَارِّهِمْ. (IAar, TA.)
مَكَّانُ: see مَصَّانٌ in art. مص.
مَكَانَةٌ Greatness, and high rank or standing. in the estimation of the Sultán: (Msb:) an honourable place in the estimation of a king. (K.)
جَلَسَ مُتَمَكِّنًا He sat in a firm, or settled, posture; as when one sits cross-legged.

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
